title: Insurance retreat and climate risk modeling
bottleneck: Insurers are withdrawing from fire- and flood-prone regions because catastrophe models cannot price accelerating climate risk: historical loss data no longer predicts future losses, correlated extremes break diversification assumptions, and granular forward-looking models do not exist at the parcel level. The result is an insurance death spiral — withdrawal raises uninsured losses, which raises risk, which accelerates withdrawal. Mortgage markets built on mandatory insurance face systemic risk.
why_it_blocks: Insurance is the financial infrastructure of homeownership and much commercial lending; its retreat strands trillions in assets and pushes costs onto taxpayers via insurer-of-last-resort schemes. The modeling gap turns a risk-transfer problem into a financial stability problem.
current_state: Parametric insurance and public reinsurance backstops are expanding, and catastrophe modeling is incorporating climate projections. But no model yet credibly prices 2050-era extremes at property scale, and retreat is outpacing model improvement.
